name: Spuyten Duyvil Bridge
facts: Spuyten Duyvil Bridge, built in 1900 by engineer Robert Giles, features a 290‑foot swing span that swivels nearly 65 degrees, offering 100 feet of clearance on each side for passing vessels.
After a 1982 vessel collision left the swing span stuck open, Amtrak rehabilitated the bridge in the late 1980s, enabling the Empire Connection to route trains from Penn Station to Albany.
In June 2018, the Left Coast Lifter lifted the bridge’s 1.6‑million‑pound spans onto a barge to repair Hurricane Sandy damage, temporarily diverting trains to Grand Central.
